output:
I ran `/code-conventions --review-pr` on `c66f89e2...HEAD`. It's one commit (`dd402c04a`) that changes 3 doc files (+6/−1) and no code. I found 3 problems with the cited evidence and 3 smaller wording gaps. None of it is blocking, but the first finding would teach a wrong precedent.

**How I ran it**
- The checklist script wrote all 47 rules to my scratchpad instead of the repo. I didn't modify, create or delete any tracked files, and I didn't run tests, installs or `gh`.
- I worked through every rule. Since the diff is guidance text only, the rules that applied were CHANGE-01, CHANGE-02, CHANGE-04, PR-02, MOD-01 and PR-01. The rest had nothing to check.
- I checked each claim the new text makes against `src/`.
- I didn't need to look up past review learnings for any rule.
- The new SPDX headers are fine: all 3 files already have the `.md` license header.

## Findings

**1. The examples given for "reached through another module" mostly don't fit the rule** (medium; PR-02)
`docs/agents/module-structure.md:133` says a module may skip registering in `app.module.ts` "when the new module only serves that one". It then says `backbone`, `email`, `siwe` and `queues` "are wired the same way". The code says otherwise for three of the four:
- **`siwe`** serves two modules: `src/modules/auth/auth.module.ts:6` and `src/modules/users/users.module.ts:6`.
- **`queues`** serves two modules through two different sub-modules: `QueuesApiModule` in `src/modules/health/health.module.ts:7` and `QueuesRepositoryModule` in `src/modules/hooks/hooks.module.ts:9`.
- **`email`** has no module of its own. It is two separate providers: `src/modules/email/pushwoosh/pushwoosh-email.module.ts`, used by `alerts.module.ts:20`, and `src/modules/email/ses/ses-email.module.ts`, used by `spaces.module.ts:9`.
- **`backbone`** (only `chains.module.ts:6`) and `EntitlementsModule` (only `src/modules/billing/billing.module.ts:18`) are the only accurate examples.

Fix: drop "only serves that one" and say "is only consumed by already-registered modules", or keep just `backbone` and `EntitlementsModule` as the examples.

**2. The new registration rule doesn't mention feature-flag inheritance** (medium; MOD-01)
At `module-structure.md:133`, `BillingModule` is only loaded when its flag is on (`src/app.module.ts:97`), so `EntitlementsModule` quietly sits behind the billing flag too.
- The text doesn't mention this. If a second module later imports `EntitlementsModule`, it gets loaded even when billing is switched off. MOD-01 forbids exactly that ("do not bypass an existing feature flag by importing a gated module unconditionally").
- Fix: add one sentence saying the imported module gets the parent's flag gating, and importing it anywhere else must keep that gating.

**3. The "self-contained HTTP surface" test is unclear for `EntitlementsModule`** (low; PR-02)
The same line ends "A module with its own HTTP surface registers directly".
- `src/modules/entitlements/routes/` exists, holding `entitlements.service.ts` and `subscription-sync.service.ts`, but has no controller.
- Taken together with the new rule at `module-structure.md:33` (`routes/` may arrive one PR before its controller), it's unclear whether `EntitlementsModule` must move to `app.module.ts` once its controller lands.
- Fix: say explicitly that when a staged module gains its controller, its registration moves to `app.module.ts`.

**4. The two guides set different evidence bars for "declared series"** (low; PR-02)
- `module-structure.md:33` requires the PR description to "link the follow-up PR that adds the controller".
- `docs/agents/reviewing.md:48` only requires it to "state which follow-up consumes it".
- Reviewers applying the two guides will judge the same PR differently. Pick one wording and use it in both places.

**5. The in-place removal exception doesn't say which environment's flag counts** (low; CHANGE-04)
`docs/agents/api-dtos-and-validation.md:113` allows removing or renaming a field in place when its endpoint "has sat behind a disabled feature flag since it was introduced".
- Flags differ per environment. A flag that's off in production may be on in staging or dev, where real clients have already parsed the field.
- Fix: say "disabled in every environment serving released clients", or name production explicitly.

**6. The commit subject leaves out one of its three changes** (low; CHANGE-02)
- Commit `dd402c04a` is titled "codify staged delivery and transitive module registration".
- It also adds an unrelated API-versioning exception at `api-dtos-and-validation.md:113`.
- Since `main` is squash-merged, the PR title becomes the only record. Either mention it in the title and Summary, or move it to its own PR.

All six fixes are edits to the new guide text.
